title: Using Large Language Models to Provide Explanatory Feedback to Human Tutors
extended_summary:
This paper addresses how large language models (LLMs) might support automatic explanatory feedback in online tutor-training lessons. The central problem is that novice tutors need timely, specific feedback on their responses to constructed-response questions, but manually providing such feedback at scale is difficult. The authors focus on whether machine learning can identify effective versus ineffective praise and then use those predictions to generate feedback that explains why a tutor response is appropriate or not.

The proposed approach combines binary classification with named entity recognition (NER). First, the authors annotate tutor responses from an online lesson on giving effective praise and train BERT-based classifiers to detect effort-based and outcome-based praise. Second, they use NER to highlight the relevant parts of tutor responses so they can be inserted into template-based explanatory feedback. The study uses 65 volunteer tutors and 129 tutor responses from the “Giving Effective Praise” lesson, an online scenario-based tutor-training context.

Results suggest that BERT can identify effort-based praise reasonably well, but performs much more weakly on outcome-based praise. The NER approach also shows limited performance, though it can sometimes correctly identify relevant praise spans and support feedback generation. The paper concludes that LLM-facilitated classification and NER are promising for automated tutor feedback, but that the current approach is constrained by small and imbalanced data and would benefit from more annotation, better evaluation metrics, and improved models before practical deployment.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a workshop/work-in-progress paper with a small annotated dataset and model-development focus, not a controlled impact study. It reports algorithmic performance metrics rather than a rigorous evaluation of educational outcomes or comparative effectiveness.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper suggests potentially useful automation for tutor feedback, but it does not demonstrate measurable impact on tutor performance or student outcomes. Any practical effect is therefore modest and still uncertain.

interventions.use_case: BERT/LLM-assisted automatic classification and named-entity recognition to provide real-time explanatory feedback to novice tutors composing responses in an online lesson on giving effective praise.

finding.finding_summary: The paper reports that the proposed LLM/BERT-based feedback system can support tutors’ learning by identifying effective praise components and highlighting relevant text spans for explanatory feedback. In the authors’ framing, this is intended to improve tutor reasoning about praise quality and help novice tutors revise responses more effectively, but no causal learner-outcome evaluation was conducted.
finding.measure: Model performance for classifying praise types and tagging named entities used to generate explanatory feedback
finding.std_deviation: Classification SD for Effort F1=0.046; Outcome F1=0.235; NER SD=0.039

finding.finding_summary: The system is presented as a way to deliver timely, specific, and scalable corrective/explanatory feedback to tutors, reducing reliance on human feedback generation. However, the paper does not report direct measurements of planning speed, workload reduction, or uptake of feedback in authentic use; the evidence is limited to automated classification and NER performance.
finding.measure: Automated classification accuracy/F1 and NER F1 as proxies for feedback automation capability
finding.std_deviation: Outcome classification SD=0.235; Effort classification SD=0.046; NER SD=0.039
